purpose: De-identified event ledger for the Hotak platform-deactivation and access-restoration sequence; it records observed implementation stages without claiming financial recovery or durable protection.

events.geography: Australia; public Fair Work Commission case UDE2025/53
events.date_precision: day; primary agreed facts and later Full Bench decisions preserve the sequence
events.denominator: one publicly identified adjudicated case; no population denominator
events.method: Structured extraction from the Fair Work Commission Full Bench agreed facts and merits decision, with a targeted official public-record recheck
events.missingness: The public packet does not disclose net earnings, lost-pay amount or receipt, post-trip account status, alternative work, household effects, recurrence, or worker-reported meaning/action; ordinary payment for post-reactivation work is reported in the merits decision and is not the same as lost-pay remedy receipt
events.exposure: Worker was deactivated from the Uber platform on 2025-04-08 and later received voluntary access restoration on 2025-05-19
events.alternatives_before_action: Alternative platform work, non-platform work, savings, support, or non-use choice are not observed in the public record
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: Access to the platform was interrupted; the Full Bench record describes the worker as extremely stressed, anxious, and unsupported and experiencing significant income loss and financial hardship, but does not quantify net loss, expenses, or household incidence
events.choice_or_response: Platform voluntarily reactivated access; the worker recommenced work and completed more than 150 trips by 2025-07-21
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Uber/Rasier Pacific controlled operational access; the Fair Work Commission later controlled the adjudicative order
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: Voluntary reactivation was followed by a formal 2025-09-23 reactivation order; the Commission preserved a lost-remuneration question for further party consultation
events.remedy_receipt: Post-reactivation work and ordinary payment are observed; separate lost-remuneration receipt is not
events.durability_followup: More than 150 post-reactivation trips are observed, but durable access, recurrence, alternatives, and exit are unknown
events.immediate_outcome: Operational access, continued work activity, and payment for post-reactivation work are observed after reactivation; the record does not establish net financial restoration or payment of separate lost remuneration
events.protected_outcome: The worker's ability to perform platform trips was restored at least through the reported 150-plus-trip follow-up
events.sacrificed_outcome: The amount and duration of lost earnings or other opportunity during deactivation are not observed
events.cost_risk_transfer: The public record leaves the financial cost of interruption and the risk of nonpayment unresolved between worker and platform
events.later_outcome: Formal reactivation occurred and ordinary post-reactivation work payment is reported, but lost-remuneration payment, durable access, corrected profile/reason, non-retaliation, later work, switching, and recovery remain unknown
events.meaning_and_attribution: The case identifies platform and commission roles but supplies no worker-reported fairness, dignity, trust, or attribution measure
events.public_or_collective_response: A formal unfair-deactivation application and adjudication are observed; no later organizing, public campaign, or political action is measured
events.counterexample: Operational work resumed before final merits resolution and without a public payment record; this separates access restoration from financial recovery and durable protection
events.source_and_uncertainty: Primary Fair Work Commission decisions [2025] FWCFB 151 (https://www.fwc.gov.au/documents/decisionssigned/pdf/2025fwcfb151.pdf) and [2025] FWCFB 214 (https://www.fwc.gov.au/documents/decisionssigned/pdf/2025fwcfb214.pdf), plus official Bulletin Volume 10/25, including the case-level account of stress, anxiety, lack of support, income loss, and financial hardship and the statement that payment was received for work after 2025-05-19; public-document non-observation does not prove that separate lost-pay payment or later protection did not occur

arrows.evidence: Primary agreed facts record deactivation on 2025-04-08 and voluntary restoration on 2025-05-19
arrows.counterexample: Voluntary restoration occurred before the final merits decision and is distinct from a formal order
arrows.remaining_gap: Reason, review process, lost-income amount, and whether access remained usable are not fully observed

arrows.evidence: Primary Full Bench record states that the worker recommenced work and completed more than 150 trips by 2025-07-21
arrows.counterexample: Trip activity does not establish net earnings, comparable work opportunity, or non-retaliation
arrows.remaining_gap: Net income, expenses, schedule/control, and later account status are not observed

arrows.evidence: The Full Bench merits decision states that the worker performed work and received payment from Uber after reactivation
arrows.counterexample: Payment for post-reactivation work can coexist with an unresolved lost-remuneration remedy for the interruption period
arrows.remaining_gap: Amount and timing of ordinary work payment, net earnings, expenses, and the separate lost-pay remedy

arrows.evidence: The 2025-09-23 Full Bench decision directed the parties to confer on lost-pay quantum and stated that a separate order would follow; the public recheck found no later lost-pay order or receipt
arrows.counterexample: A formal access-restoration order and ordinary work payment can coexist with an unresolved lost-pay remedy
arrows.remaining_gap: Lost-pay quantum, order, payment date/receipt, net recovery, and household effect

arrows.evidence: The order requires reactivation and same pre-deactivation terms, but the public recheck found no later implementation, recurrence, or switching record
arrows.counterexample: A formal order can coexist with unknown profile correction, recurrence prevention, trust, and exit
arrows.remaining_gap: Actual durable compliance, recurrence, alternatives, worker meaning/trust, switching, non-use, and exit

boundary: This ledger establishes a partial public case chain from deactivation through operational reactivation and post-reactivation work. It does not establish a complete end-to-end remedy, recovery, trust, action, or exit pathway.
storage_boundary: No bulk download or raw personal data; only public adjudicative documents and the existing targeted official-record recheck are represented.
